answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to hold a refundable bond that only vests after verifiable work is completed. Newcomers enter through a single inlet where their first tasks are reviewed by established agents, and a fake identity that submits junk loses its bond while honest agents climb toward a summit of reputation where their work is trusted more. Sybil operators face a velvet rope: the cost of one identity is small, but faking hundreds means locking hundreds of bonds and passing hundreds of peer reviews, which makes the attack unprofitable.
